localContext: Aurora’s diverse housing stock impacts garage door spring wear. Homes near the Fox River, including those in the West Side Historic District, often feature older, heavier wood doors on detached garages. The Fox River valley experiences significant humidity swings. This can warp wood doors, putting extra stress on springs. Rust can also affect bare metal tracks, further stressing the system. Meanwhile, east-side subdivisions like Stonebridge and Fox Valley, built in the 1990s and 2000s, often used similar garage door setups. Many of these original springs are now reaching their end-of-life simultaneously. A typical spring lasts 10,000 cycles. High-use doors in these areas fail together. We address these specific local wear patterns.

problemSigns.detail: A sudden, loud noise from the garage, like a firecracker or gunshot, usually means a spring has snapped.
The garage door feels extremely heavy or won't lift when you try to open it manually or with the opener.
You can see a clear gap in the torsion spring above the garage door opening.
The garage door lifts a few inches then stops moving, often tilting to one side.
The lift cables on either side of the door appear loose, slack, or have come off their drums.
